requirement:
Habeas's bundled agent skills MUST direct agents to choose references by the
procedure in {cite}`requirements.references.procedure`. For internal code, they
MUST direct agents to state any invariant worth checking as an ordinary
requirement and implement it, to cite the built-in `habeas:util` under
{cite}`requirements.references.util` on an item that only serves other code, and
to report to the user an item that does neither. They MUST
NOT suggest grouping requirements, such as `internal.config_parsing`, that state
no checkable obligation.
rationale:
I found no gap. I did not read the other bundled skills or the `SKILLS` constant directly. The test asserts over every entry in `SKILLS`, so I relied on it for the "no grouping" check across skills.

The subject's obligations map to the bundled skill text as follows.

- **Choose references by `requirements.references.procedure`.** `assets/skills/habeas-requirements/SKILL.md` has a "Choosing references" section that follows the procedure's steps in order:
  - `{test}` for a test designed to verify the definition.
  - `{impl}` for a root.
  - `{cite}` for code that should be re-checked when the definition changes.
  - `` // {cite}`habeas:util` `` for an item that serves other code and carries out no requirement.
  - The "Choosing references" text defines a root and says that code a root reaches needs no reference.
  - `assets/skills/habeas-evidence/SKILL.md` ("Uncovered Rust items") and `assets/skills/habeas-bootstrap-requirements/SKILL.md` ("Tagging") point to that section instead of restating it.

- **State an invariant worth checking as an ordinary requirement and implement it.** The "Edge cases" list in `habeas-requirements` says to propose a requirement stating the invariant and `{impl}` it. The bootstrap skill's "Proposing requirements" says to write a requirement for the invariant rather than inventing a user-facing promise.

- **Cite `habeas:util` on an item that only serves other code.** This is step 4 of "Choosing references" in `habeas-requirements`. It is also a row in the situation table under "Uncovered Rust items" in `habeas-evidence`. The "Gotchas" section in `habeas-requirements` says to author first, because reads cover items before `habeas:util` is considered. This matches step 4 of the procedure.

- **Report to the user an item that does neither.** `habeas-requirements` says to report it with a proposed requirement, or as dead code if nothing reaches it, and not to delete it unasked. `habeas-evidence` covers dead code in the same way. The bootstrap skill puts such an item on the gap list.

- **MUST NOT suggest grouping requirements that state no checkable obligation.** `habeas-requirements` says "Don't propose grouping requirements that state no checkable obligation". No bundled skill suggests grouping, `internal.config_parsing`, or catch-all requirements, and none offers a waiver; the test asserts this for every skill in `SKILLS`.

Tests: `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[bundled_skills_direct_the_reference_procedure_and_report_items_without_one]` carries `{test}` for this requirement. It asserts these points:
- The procedure steps appear in order in `habeas-requirements`.
- The `habeas-evidence` and `habeas-bootstrap-requirements` skills refer to the procedure rather than restate it.
- The invariant, `habeas:util` and report-to-user guidance is present.
- The grouping and waiver phrases are absent from every skill.

`tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[bundled_skills_mark_roots_and_handle_uncovered_items]` also carries `{test}`. It additionally covers the `habeas:util` and dead-code report rows in `habeas-evidence`.

Reachability: the three `SKILL.md` files are the `{impl}` items, and nothing else implements the requirement. The skills' other content is not extra behavior of this subject.

text: :::{req} internal_detail_guidance
Habeas's bundled agent skills MUST direct agents to choose references by the
procedure in {cite}`requirements.references.procedure`. For internal code, they
MUST direct agents to state any invariant worth checking as an ordinary
requirement and implement it, to cite the built-in `habeas:util` under
{cite}`requirements.references.util` on an item that only serves other code, and
to report to the user an item that does neither. They MUST
NOT suggest grouping requirements, such as `internal.config_parsing`, that state
no checkable obligation.
:::{req} procedure
A source item MUST choose its references under {cite}`requirements.references.roles`
for each candidate definition by this procedure, and MAY carry several:
1. If the item is a test designed to verify the definition, it MUST use
`{test}`. A test helper a reviewer reaches by following such a test needs no
reference to the definition.
2. Otherwise, if the item is a root of the definition's implementation, it
MUST use `{impl}`. Code or a type carries out part of a definition when it
makes a decision, performs a check, produces an output, or handles a case
the definition specifies, or when the definition constrains its shape:
fields, variants, serialized form, or validation. A root is such an item
that no other item marked `{impl}` for the definition reaches, where an item
reaches what it calls, the types it uses, and the implementations of trait
methods it calls, and what those reach in turn. An item reached from a root
needs no reference to the definition. An item that is a site of a distributed definition
under {cite}`requirements.references.distributed` needs no reference to it;
its site review covers it.
3. Otherwise, if the item should be re-checked or kept in sync when the
definition changes, it MUST use `{cite}`.
4. If the item carries no reference after applying steps 1 to 3 to every
definition and no assessment reads it under
{cite}`requirements.references.rust_item_coverage`, it MUST cite the
built-in `habeas:util` under {cite}`requirements.references.util` when it
serves other code. An item that does neither carries out behavior that needs
a requirement, or is not needed.
A `{fixme}` reference is added independently of this procedure, and MUST NOT
count as an item's reference for {cite}`requirements.references.rust_item_coverage`.
:::{req} util
Habeas MUST provide the built-in `habeas:util` under
{cite}`requirements.references.builtin_definitions`, with this text:
> Cite this on an item that serves other code, including code outside the
> project such as a library calling a trait implementation it requires, and
> carries out no requirement or example itself: it has no obligations and no
> end-user-observable behavior of its own. A review that reaches it from a root judges what it does
> as part of that root.
Only `{cite}` MAY reference it, inline or fenced, with or without commentary. An
item whose only citations are of `habeas:util` MUST NOT need a citation review
under {cite}`requirements.references.citation_review`. A citation of
`habeas:util` MUST cover its item under
{cite}`requirements.references.rust_item_coverage`.
